definition: Participative research is a research approach that includes participants’ own views and experiences as part of the study, often through qualitative data. It helps make findings or interventions better matched to people’s needs and preferences.

reasons: The packet supports only that participative research will contribute qualitative data; it does not define the term as including participants’ own views and experiences.

The claim that it helps make findings or interventions better matched to people’s needs and preferences is broader than the packet supports, which only says the study was designed to tailor interventions to individual needs and preferences.

The packet only states that “participative research will contribute valuable qualitative data” and that the study includes “patients’ views on falls prevention.” It does not explicitly support the claim that participative research “helps make findings or interventions better matched to people’s needs and preferences.”

The definition says participative research “often” uses qualitative data; the packet mentions qualitative data in this specific study but does not establish that this is an “often” general characteristic of the approach.
